independent_unique_answer_proof.method: Visually compared actual source JPG, formal PNG and native candidate at their actual resolutions. Independently translated the given and each option by their own head centers, then compared all six preexisting anatomical objects, rather than relying on stored answer or primary proof.
independent_unique_answer_proof.invariants: The oval head is 2.2 by 2; outer ear triangles and white inner ear boundaries, nose type/location/size and handedness must be preserved when eyes are added. All five choices have the same two eye polygons, so eye shapes do not discriminate.

elimination.A: Outer/inner ears and head match, but the downward nose begins 0.2 units above the original nose base and is taller: vertices (-0.2,0.2),(0.2,0.2),(0,-0.4), versus original (-0.2,0),(0.2,0),(0,-0.34). Actual source and native images show the elongated nose; adding eyes cannot cause this.
elimination.B: All six existing objects match after translation, including the two white triangles, the downward small triangular nose and their relative placement. Hence B is the unique option preserving existing anatomical features.
elimination.C: Head, outer ears and nose match, but each white-ear upper corner is lower and slightly inward. Left original (-0.82,1.18) becomes (-0.8,0.99); right original (0.82,1.18) becomes (0.8,0.99), with fixed lower/inner vertices. The source JPG shows a sloping original/B shoulder and a much flatter, lower C shoulder; native pixels confirm it. Eye addition cannot alter those preexisting white regions.
elimination.D: Ear/head features match, but the nose triangle points upward and is shifted: base y=-0.3, apex y=0.04. It does not preserve the original downward nose.
elimination.E: Ear/head features match, but the original triangle has been replaced by a radius-0.2 disk centered at (0,-0.12).

mouth_and_exact_completion_wording.geometry: Two quarter-circle arcs of radius 0.55, centered locally at (-0.55,-0.34) and (0.55,-0.34), meeting at the nose tip. They are present in the actual source choices and formal choices, absent from the given; no candidate action adds or edits them.
mouth_and_exact_completion_wording.disposition: This is a preexisting source-wording looseness, not an effect of this variant. If only eyes literally may be added and absolutely nothing else, none of the options is an exact eyes-only extension, since every option also contains mouth arcs. Under the natural finished-drawing reading allowing those common mouth details while preserving existing anatomy, B uniquely survives. I do not silently claim exact eyes-only pixel equivalence or use a mouth difference to eliminate a choice.

independent_unique_answer_proof.answer_of_annotated_image_without_annota: No unconditional unique answer established. B is recovered only if the viewer knows the red/blue ear edges are comparison annotations to ignore as original drawing content.

actual_visual_inspection.readability_findings: The 2 pt strokes are about 2.78 px on heads about 62.46 px wide. The diagnostic corner-height change is about 5.39 px, so it is not erased wholesale. The original sloping red/blue edges and C's almost horizontal ones can still be seen, especially in isolated native crops. However, the stroke occupies part of each small white interior, and the immediate visual signal is matching red-left/blue-right cat-ear ink. Magnified crops explain the pixels; they are not evidence of effortless normal-size recognition.
actual_visual_inspection.text_fill_and_foreground: A-E labels, all noses, eye polygons, mouth curves and head outlines are unchanged outside the four ear regions. No new closed contour, separate ink island, crosscut, equality glyph or eye is introduced.

human_semantics_disposition.not_a_blanket_color_rule: Authorized style marks do not automatically become mathematical givens. In a geometry relation problem these strokes could simply identify two edges. This task instead asks whether an unfinished drawing is preserved as it is completed; colored ink on its ear boundaries is itself a plausible drawing detail.
human_semantics_disposition.annotation_reading: A reader informed of the Special comparison convention can ignore color as source content, compare the white ear regions, reject C and recover B.
human_semantics_disposition.drawing_content_reading: An ordinary reader sees red on the given left ear and blue on the right, with matching colors only in C. No legend, separate annotation layer label or request sentence says to exclude these features when checking preservation. Such a reader reasonably judges plain-black B as having lost existing ink. Exact preservation still rejects C for the lower ear shoulders, producing no exact match; coarse feature reading instead favors C.
human_semantics_disposition.why_decisive: The candidate therefore requires an unstated choice of what counts as the given drawing. The raw answers illustrate that ambiguity but do not prove geometry or establish human prevalence. My rejection rests on the actual image and wording, not a model narrative, a numeric mark cap, or a general ban on selective color.

    *   There is a centered face sticker (let's call its side length $x$).
    *   There are four edge stickers along the four sides of this face (part of them are visible on the face, part on the edge). These edge stickers appear as squares on the face.
    *   Since the stickers meet at their corners, the distance from the center of the face to the corner of the central sticker plus the diagonal side of the edge sticker arrangement covers the distance to the corner of the cube face.
    *   Specifically, if we look at a face, the central square ($x \times x$) is in the middle, and four other squares are in the corners of the face. For these squares to touch at their corners along the edge of the face, and considering the symmetry, the sum of the two side lengths ($x + x$) must equal the total width of the face ($10 \mathrm{~cm}$).
    *   Therefore, $2x = 10 \mathrm{~cm}$, which means the side length of each sticker is $x = 5 \mathrm{~cm}$.

3.  **Calculate Areas**:
    *   **Area of one sticker**: $A = 5 \mathrm{~cm} \times 5 \mathrm{~cm} = 25 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$.
